\section*{Question 6}

Let \(f\) be the function defined by
\[
f(x)= \begin{cases}\sqrt{x+1} & \text { for } 0 \leq x \leq 3 \\ 5-x & \text { for } 3<x \leq 5 .\end{cases}
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Is \(f\) continuous at \(x=3\) ? Explain why or why not.
\item[(b)] Find the average value of \(f(x)\) on the closed interval \(0 \leq x \leq 5\).
\item[(c)] Suppose the function \(g\) is defined by
\[
g(x)= \begin{cases}k \sqrt{x+1} & \text { for } 0 \leq x \leq 3 \\ m x+2 & \text { for } 3<x \leq 5,\end{cases}
\]
where \(k\) and \(m\) are constants. If \(g\) is differentiable at \(x=3\), what are the values of \(k\) and \(m\) ?
\item[(a)] \(f\) is continuous at \(x=3\) because
\[
\lim _{x \rightarrow 3^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 3^{+}} f(x)=2 .
\]
Therefore, \(\lim _{x \rightarrow 3} f(x)=2=f(3)\).
\item[(b)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_{0}^{5} f(x) d x & =\int_{0}^{3} f(x) d x+\int_{3}^{5} f(x) d x \\
& =\left.\frac{2}{3}(x+1)^{3 / 2}\right|_{0} ^{3}+\left.\left(5 x-\frac{1}{2} x^{2}\right)\right|_{3} ^{5} \\
& =\left(\frac{16}{3}-\frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(\frac{25}{2}-\frac{21}{2}\right)=\frac{20}{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
Average value: \(\frac{1}{5} \int_{0}^{5} f(x) d x=\frac{4}{3}\)
\item[(c)] Since \(g\) is continuous at \(x=3,2 k=3 m+2\).
\[
\begin{aligned}
& g^{\prime}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}
\frac{k}{2 \sqrt{x+1}} & \text { for } 0<x<3 \\
m & \text { for } 3<x<5
\end{array}\right. \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 3^{-}} g^{\prime}(x)=\frac{k}{4} \text { and } \lim _{x \rightarrow 3^{+}} g^{\prime}(x)=m
\end{aligned}
\]
Since these two limits exist and \(g\) is
differentiable at \(x=3\), the two limits are
equal. Thus \(\frac{k}{4}=m\).
\[
8 m=3 m+2 ; m=\frac{2}{5} \text { and } k=\frac{8}{5}
\]
\end{itemize}
